batches.description: Baseline at commit 961231e, before read exploration existed: read had no depth/pattern/regex arguments and the system prompt still suggested bash for ls/find/rg/grep. All 7 denials were exploratory shell commands (ls/cat/rg/grep).

deniedCommands: cat -A input.txt; echo "---"; cat verify.cjs; echo "---"; ls -la
ls -la && cat -A input.txt && echo "---VERIFY---" && cat verify.cjs
ls -la; echo ---; cat verify.cjs; echo ---; cat untouched.txt
ls -la; echo '---'; cat settings.json 2>/dev/null; echo '---'; cat defaults.json 2>/dev/null; echo '---'; cat verify.cjs 2>/dev/null | head -100
rg -n "hello" greeting.txt guide.txt; cat -A keep.txt; echo; echo "---"; cat greeting.txt; echo "---"; cat guide.txt
grep -n "hello" greeting.txt guide.txt; echo "---"; cat -A keep.txt; echo "---"; cat greeting.txt; echo "---"; cat guide.txt

batches.description: Batch A at commit 17a6e59, after read gained depth/pattern/regex exploration but before the system prompt was aligned: the prompt still told the model to use bash for ls/find/rg/grep, conflicting with the new tool descriptions.

Batch B at commit 3b4d301, after both the tool descriptions (b41d75f) and the system prompt (3b4d301) steered the model toward read exploration. Review fixes for bounded walking, VM-isolated regex and prompt alignment are included.

countingRule: A read call counts as exploration when its arguments contain a non-null pattern or a non-null depth. Denials, approvals, token sums and durations are computed from the raw per-attempt records in each source file; all input/output usage breakdowns were available (no estimates).
note: Three sequential 45-attempt cohorts (5 fixtures x 3 modes x 3 repetitions) on the same fixtures, budgets and execution order as the configured-vLLM baseline. Denials dropped from 7 to 1 only after both the tool descriptions and the system prompt were aligned (commits b41d75f and 3b4d301); an intermediate batch after the description change alone was stopped after 23 attempts (23 passed, 4 denials) when the prompt conflict was discovered, its file was deleted and it is not a sample. Input tokens and wall time rose versus the baseline because listing/search results enter the context and tool descriptions are longer. All 45 attempts in the tuned batch passed the execution-order, mutation-scope, verification, protected-file and output checks (unmetRequirements empty). A small finite sample does not prove general reliability or a cost benefit. An independent final-reply review is being written to repeated-tasks-iter4-explore-tuned-response-review.json. CI has not run for these commits and nothing is merged or released.
